facts_of_case: Parties were married in 2020; no child born; petitioner-wife living separately since 2022 and seeking transfer of respondent-husband's petition under Section 13 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955.

legal_principles.principle: The cardinal principle for exercise of power under section 24 of the Code of Civil Procedure is that the ends of justice should demand the transfer of the suit, appeal or other proceeding.
legal_principles.held: The Hon'ble Supreme Court has held as under: '9. The cardinal principle for exercise of power under section 24 of the Code of Civil Procedure is that the ends of justice should demand the transfer of the suit, appeal or other proceeding.'
cited_cases: N.C.V. Aishwarya vs A.S. Saravana Karthik Sha, (2022) Live Law (SC) 627

legal_principles.principle: In matrimonial matters, wherever Courts are called upon to consider the plea of transfer, the Courts have to take into consideration the economic soundness of both the parties, the social strata of the spouses and their behavioural pattern.
legal_principles.held: The Hon'ble Supreme Court has held as under: '9. The cardinal principle for exercise of power under section 24 of the Code of Civil Procedure is that the ends of justice should demand the transfer of the suit, appeal or other proceeding.'
cited_cases: N.C.V. Aishwarya vs A.S. Saravana Karthik Sha, (2022) Live Law (SC) 627

legal_principles.principle: Given the prevailing socioeconomic paradigm in the Indian society, generally, it is the wife's convenience which must be looked at while considering transfer.
legal_principles.held: The Hon'ble Supreme Court has held as under: '9. The cardinal principle for exercise of power under section 24 of the Code of Civil Procedure is that the ends of justice should demand the transfer of the suit, appeal or other proceeding.'
cited_cases: N.C.V. Aishwarya vs A.S. Saravana Karthik Sha, (2022) Live Law (SC) 627

legal_principles.principle: While deciding the transfer application, the Courts are required to give more weightage and consideration to the convenience of the female litigants.
legal_principles.held: The Hon'ble Supreme Court has observed that 'while deciding the transfer application, the Courts are required to give more weightage and consideration to the convenience of the female litigants.'

Rajani Kishor Pardeshi vs Kishor Babulal Pardeshi, (2005) (12) SCC 237

outcome.final_order: Petition for transfer of case allowed.
